data.segment_title: Campaign 2008 / Obama vs. McCain / The Campaign / Voting
data.segment_description:
(Studio: Katie Couric) The home stretch for Senators Barack Obama and John McCain introduced; map shown of their planned campaign stops.  

(Columbus, Ohio: Chip Reid) The McCain campaign’s focus on Ohio and Pennsylvania featured; statistics on visits since Monday by McCain and Governor Sarah Palin and their opponents compared; findings of independent polls showing Obama leading in both states cited; scenes shown of McCain in Columbus with California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger. [In Ohio, McCAIN – campaigns.] [Senator Lindsey GRAHAM†- says the road to the White House runs through Ohio.] [In Pennsylvania, PALIN – campaigns.] [SCHWARZENEGGER – says McCain is a real action hero.] The announcement from former Reagan chief of staff Ken Duberstein†† that he intends to vote for Obama noted.  

(Studio: Katie Couric) McCain’s plan to return to New Hampshire noted.  

(Chicago: Dean Reynolds) Obama’s return to Iowa, where his campaign was launched, reviewed; ads and map shown; scenes shown of former Vice President Al Gore in Florida and Senator Hillary Clinton in Ohio campaigning for Obama. [In Des Moines, OBAMA – says what you started in Iowa has swept the nation.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric) Statistics on early voting cited.  

(New York: Armen Keteyian) Anxiety about the ability of the voting system to handle the crowds that are expected to vote on Tuesday examined; scenes shown of early voting lines in Florida; map shown of voting machine allocation; details given about provisional ballots. [2 early VOTERS – comment on the long lines.] [Advancement Project Judith BROWNE-DIANIS†- notes many election officials lack the resources for an efficient election.] [Common Cause vice president for research Tova WANG†- comments on uncertainty about machines.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric) Obama’s strength in the Western battleground states of Nevada, Colorado and New Mexico noted; poll findings cited.  

(Espanola, New Mexico: Jeff Greenfield) Obama’s position in the West examined; details given about demographics and geography; statistics on Hispanic voters cited. [University of New Mexico Christine SIERRA†- comments on the importance of jobs and the economy to Hispanics.] [In Espanola, New Mexico, last month, OBAMA – urges Hispanics to vote.] [Espanola Mayor Joseph MAESTAS†- notes Obama has 4 times more offices than McCain.] [Obama supporter Albert CATA†- explains why they want to get involved.] [McCain supporter Cecilia MARTINEZ SALAZAR†- comments on the conservative values of many Hispanics.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric, Bob Schieffer) The toxic environment for Republicans and the fact that President Bush has not appeared at one rally for any Republican candidate this year discussed. This week’s “Face the Nation” lineup noted.
(Studio: Katie Couric) The announcement from JPMorgan Chase of a 90-day freeze on foreclosures noted.

(Studio: Katie Couric) Report introduced.  

(White House: Jim Axelrod) President Bush’s push to change regulations before he leaves office featured; details given of plans involving rules on mining, air pollution and clean water at factory farms; Bush’s 11th hour regulation changes and President Bill Clinton’s compared. [White House deputy press secretary Tony FRATTO†- states we were trying to avoid charges that we were rushing regulations into place in the dark of night.] [OMB Watch Matt MADIA†- says the rules are going to be to the benefit of industry.]

(Sioux Falls, South Dakota: Kelly Cobiella) The battle over South Dakota’s Initiative 11, which would make abortion a crime in most cases, featured; details given of Colorado’s proposed amendment to define a fertilized human egg as a person. [At Planned Parenthood, in shadow, 18-year-old GIRL – explains why she is seeking an abortion.] [Vote Yes for Life executive director Leslee UNRUH†- says she believes Roe v. Wade will be over.] [“Argus Leader” managing editor Patrick LALLEY†- notes people who voted against a ban in 2006 would vote for it if it had exceptions.] [Planned Parenthood South Dakota president Sarah STOESZ†- worries other states will enact abortion bans.]
(Studio: Katie Couric) The death of author Studs Terkel reported.

(Studio: Katie Couric) Report introduced.  

(Warren, Rhode Island: Steve Hartman) The competition for the heaviest pumpkin featured; scenes shown from an annual weigh-off and of a giant pumpkin being dropped by a crane. [Grower Steve CONNOLLY††- comments on his “Beast from the East."] [World record holder Joe JUTRAS††- comments on the value of champion seeds.]   

(Studio: Katie Couric, Steve Hartman) This story and next week’s segment discussed.
